request.description: Returns accessible programs. For each exercise, frontend should read effectiveSets for runtime values. If user has no override, effectiveSets == defaultSets.

Primary endpoint for workout player. Use exercise.effectiveSets for UI inputs/timers/weights. Use exercise.countdown (boolean) to choose timer vs reps screen; when true, read exercise.durationSeconds and reps (if provided).

Returns exercise metadata including admin defaultSets and quick summary fields: executionMode, countdown (boolean), reps (set_reps mode and optional for countdown), durationSeconds (countdown mode), weightKg.

item.description: Program/exercise contract: exercise blocks include executionMode + countdown(boolean) for UI mode selection, plus defaultSets and effectiveSets after applying user-specific override (if any).

item.name: Mobile App - Chat, Support & Billing Screens
Coach Chat Flow 1 - Create Or Get Thread (Auto Coach)

request.description: Step 1: Create/get chat thread for current premium user. Do not send adminId. Backend auto-assigns the single active coach/admin. After getting threadId, call socket.emit("chat:join-thread", threadId).

item.name: Coach Chat Flow 2 - Get Messages (Initial Thread Load)

request.description: Step 2: Fetch thread messages using threadId from Step 1. Each message now includes attachments[] and sender/recipient.profileImage.

formdata.value: Hello coach, please review my workout.

request.description: Step 3: Send message with optional file attachments (multipart form-data). Allowed: text only, files only, or both. On success backend emits socket event chat:message:new and chat:thread:updated.

item.name: Coach Chat Flow 4 - Mark Thread Read

request.description: Step 4: Mark unread messages in the thread as read. On success backend emits socket event chat:thread:read.

item.name: Coach Chat Flow 5 - List Threads (Inbox Refresh)

request.description: Step 5: Refresh chat inbox after sending/reading messages. Thread items include counterpart.profileImage for avatar rendering.
Creates support ticket from mobile app. Body supports email + subject + description. If email is omitted, backend falls back to authenticated user email.

item.name: Checkout Screen - Create Stripe Checkout Session

request.description: Creates Stripe Checkout Session for paid plans using webhook-first flow. Send only planKey; backend uses server-side success/cancel redirect URLs.

Reference endpoint for Stripe webhook delivery. In real use, Stripe calls this URL directly with a valid stripe-signature. For local dev, run Stripe CLI: stripe listen --forward-to {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/payments/webhook

item.description: Single-coach chat flow with realtime socket events. Socket connect: io(BASE_URL, { auth: { token: <accessToken> } }) After Step 1, join room: socket.emit("chat:join-thread", threadId) Listen events: chat:message:new, chat:thread:updated, chat:thread:read

item.name: Mobile App - Payment Flow (Webhook, 1-2-3)
item.description:
Simple subscription flow for Flutter WebView using Stripe webhook activation.
1) Create checkout session.
2) Stripe calls webhook after payment.
3) Verify billing/subscription state from API.

item.name: Payment Flow 1 - Create Checkout Session (Plan Only)

request.description: Step 1/3: Create Stripe Checkout session using only planKey. Backend handles success/cancel redirect URLs internally.
Step 2/3: Production flow is automatic (Stripe calls webhook). For local dev use Stripe CLI: stripe listen --forward-to {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/payments/webhook

item.name: Payment Flow 3 - My Payments (Verify After Webhook)

request.description: Step 3/3: Verify latest payment status after webhook delivery. Active subscription will also reflect in /api/v1/users/me.
